Cameroon is a country in Africa. It is next to the ocean.
This is Cameroon's flag: green, red and yellow stripes, with a yellow star in the middle. A flag is a symbol.

Cameroon lies where West and Central Africa meet. The Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic Ocean, is to the southwest.
Nigeria is to the northwest and Chad is to the northeast. The Central African Republic is to the east.
The Republic of the Congo is to the southeast. Gabon and Equatorial Guinea are to the south.
The Constitution names Yaoundé as the capital. Douala is a major port and economic city.
A capital is a city where important national government institutions are based. The busiest city is not automatically the capital.
The Constitution describes the flag: three equal vertical stripes of green, red and yellow. One gold star is in the centre of the red stripe.
Cameroon is divided into 10 regions. Some are Adamawa, Centre, Littoral, North West and South West.
In the south are coastal plains and dense forest. Highlands rise in the west.
In the north, savanna slopes down towards the Lake Chad basin. The land changes a lot from south to north.
Mount Cameroon is an active volcano near the coast. It is the country's highest mountain.
English and French are official languages with equal status. Many national languages are spoken too.
Cameroon has more than 200 ethnic groups. No single picture shows 'the' Cameroonian way of life.
UNESCO lists three World Heritage sites in Cameroon. One is the Dja Faunal Reserve, a protected forest area.
The others are Sangha Trinational, shared with neighbouring countries, and the Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape of the Mandara Mountains, added in 2025.

The book on the plan
A made-up story

Mina and her aunt were planning a neighbourhood library visit. Mina saw a little book on their paper plan. 'Is that a tiny building?' she asked. Her aunt pointed to the key. 'The book stands for the library.'

Mina put a counter on Start. The north arrow pointed to the top of the page. She moved one square north. There was the book. 'The symbol helped me find the place,' Mina said. They practised with the plan, not by walking alone.

Her aunt showed two paths on another plan. Mina wanted to compare them. 'Let's check what we know before deciding,' she said. The plan helped them ask a good question; it could not tell every part of the day.
What helped the characters check their idea? Think, talk with a grown-up, or skip.
Ari, Ezra and the Map of Many Places
Ari and Ezra flew to a classroom in Cameroon. The children were making a big map.
Awa drew waves for the coast. Ibrahim drew tall trees for the forest.
Esther drew green hills. Tchami drew wide grassland in the north.
'Where does each picture go?' asked Ari. Ezra flew high and pointed with his wing.
They added a key so everyone could read the map. 'One country, many places!' said Ari.
Tchami found one height for Mount Cameroon in an encyclopedia. Esther found a different height on another website.
'Which is right?' Ibrahim asked. Their teacher smiled. 'Write both, with where you found them. Then we can find out when and how each was measured, before we decide.'
Awa added a note to the map: 'Our map shows some places, not all of Cameroon.' Ari nodded. 'Good explorers show what they know and what they don't.'
Which place would you like to learn about? Think, tell a grown-up, or skip.
Why is it helpful to say where a fact came from?
